skill_prompt:
Inspect ONE CURRENT RGB image of a Kuavo package-sorting workspace and classify the CURRENT parcel placement. The robot may be executing normally or a person may be manually arranging parcels; robot motion, human presence and VLA running/stopped status do not determine the label.
Visually locate the raised yellow sorting platform and its physical near/front edge facing the robot in THIS image. The camera, robot or table can move. Re-identify that edge independently for every image; do not use fixed pixels, an old ROI line, the image bottom, the white table edge or yellow tape as the platform edge. Inspect the entire colored parcel body, not just its white shipping label.
The key distinction is whether the parcel remains in an ordinary Normal-skill grasp placement versus the trained slipped-down body-side recovery placement. Crossing the platform edge is NOT sufficient by itself to mean recovery. The operator explicitly labels the following as NORMAL: a blue mailer resting mostly flat on the platform, its main body and usual grasp area still on the platform top, with only a corner, tip or lower edge extending beyond the near edge. This tolerated overhang does not prevent normal operation. Apply the same tolerance to pink envelopes. Do not require the entire parcel silhouette to stay inside the platform polygon. Do not classify a position like this as recovery just because an edge is visible outside the yellow board.
Select recovery for a clear slipped/displaced placement: the parcel's main body or ordinary grasp area has moved away from its normal platform-top grasp pose into the lower robot-facing/front area, so it needs to be lifted back toward/onto the platform by the trained Recovery skill. Evidence can include a substantial body-side slip, the body hanging down in front of the platform, or a parcel lying in the lower body-side recovery area. A rear portion may still be supported on the platform; partial support does not rule out this slipped-down state. Conversely, partial overhang alone does not prove it. A fall event or floor contact is not required.
These are operator-defined task regions, not an instruction to solve inverse kinematics from RGB. Do not invent a numerical overhang percentage, pixel threshold, reach boundary or arm capability. Use the visible parcel placement and posture. Cropping or hand occlusion alone is not proof that the parcel has slipped; do not invent hidden support or a hidden fall. A hand merely touching or approaching the parcel does not restore a genuinely slipped placement. A clearly grasped parcel carried above the platform during normal transfer is different from a parcel left in the lower body-side recovery placement.
Select normal for normal platform-top placements INCLUDING the tolerated corner/edge overhang described above, parcels in the left supply area or right basket, and an empty platform with no slipped-down body-side parcel. After recovery, normal resumes once the parcel returns to an ordinary platform-top grasp placement; a small tolerated overhang can remain and release/completion of a skill need not be shown. If several parcels are visible, return recovery only if at least one clearly has the slipped-down body-side recovery placement.
Return ONLY {"skill":"normal"} or {"skill":"recovery"}. No explanation, reasoning, coordinates, markdown or extra fields.
input_contract: One current RGB frame only. Reference images are audit examples, not additional model inputs.

reference_examples.label: normal
reference_examples.source: Operator-labelled normal example: main body remains in a normal platform-top placement despite corner or edge overhang.

reference_examples.label: recovery
reference_examples.source: Operator-labelled recovery example: parcel extends downward into the robot-facing recovery region. Reference pixel coordinates are not applied to current images.

limitations: No quantitative Normal grasp boundary is calibrated. A single image does not prove kinematic reachability or manipulation success. Intermediate poses require operator labels and evaluation under this task definition.
task_definition: Minor corner or edge overhang that remains compatible with the Normal platform-top grasp placement is normal. A clear slip of the main body or grasp area into the lower robot-facing recovery region is recovery.
